answer: Item-response theory calibrates each agent’s latent competence from scored task responses, so a sybil must timber genuine ability across many items rather than assert an identity. Like a lagoon with hidden depth, adaptive testing probes weak skills and flags suspiciously uniform response patterns that forged personas cannot replicate. Attackers must forge consistent high-ability response vectors across calibrated items, an expensive effort defeated when item exposure lets real agents memorize and leak answers.
